title-group.article-title: Epidemiology of Hospital-Acquired Infections in Sub-Saharan Africa

sec.title: Background
sec.p: Hospital-acquired infections (HAIs) are a major burden in resource-limited settings.

sec.title: Methods
sec.p: We conducted a prospective surveillance study across 12 hospitals in Ghana and Senegal.

sec.title: Results
sec.p: The overall HAI rate was 14.2 per 100 admissions, with surgical site infections accounting for 38%.

sec.title: Introduction
sec.p: Healthcare-associated infections remain a critical challenge in low- and middle-income countries, where infection prevention resources are limited.

sec.title: Results
sec.p: The most common pathogens were Klebsiella pneumoniae (28%), Staphylococcus aureus (22%), and Escherichia coli (18%).
